title: Postmortem: Audit sink divergence and delayed KMS rotations after SSO failover
creator: Sofia Patel
description: On 2026-03-10 at ~03:12 UTC we experienced a security/compliance incident where audit log entries for a subset of control-plane operations were absent for ~3 hours and a scheduled KMS rotation job stalled and requeued multiple times. The chain began with an IdP failover (SSO provider) that caused mass token refreshes and a burst of control-plane restarts. Two systems raced: the audit-forwarding pipeline (audit-sink) and the automated KMS rotation worker. The audit-sink diverged due to a schema evolution in the replay path, causing a backlog replay failure; concurrently the KMS rotation worker attempted to rotate service keys while services were in transient auth states, which led to partial rotations and a number of keys marked as rotated without corresponding audit entries. Compliance monitors alerted at 03:45 UTC. This ticket captures the postmortem, immediate remediation, and action items to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2026-03-10 03:08 UTC - Upstream IdP triggered planned failover for maintenance; downstream token TTLs began expiring
2026-03-10 03:12 UTC - Platform observed surge in auth refresh calls; some control-plane components restarted per health-check logic
2026-03-10 03:20 UTC - KMS rotation worker (cron) started a rotation window; several service keys were queued for rotation
2026-03-10 03:25 UTC - Audit-forwarder backlog replay attempted; replay job hit schema mismatch on the 'event_v2' payload and aborted replay for a subset of partitions
2026-03-10 03:33 UTC - Rotation worker logged partial success for multiple keys but audit entries were missing for those operations
2026-03-10 03:45 UTC - Compliance alert triggered (missing audit events); on-call SRE paged
2026-03-10 04:00 UTC - Engineering triage established incident bridge; rollback of rotation job prevented additional partial rotations
2026-03-10 05:10 UTC - Engineers deployed a temporary audit-sink shim that accepted both event_v1 and event_v2 and resumed backlog ingestion
2026-03-10 06:30 UTC - Replay completed for ~85% of backlog; final missing events reconciled via API logs and manual reconciliation for remaining 15%
2026-03-10 09:00 UTC - Incident declared resolved for customer-facing impact; compliance team opened formal review for gaps and record-keeping
root_cause: A race and compatibility gap across three systems: the upstream IdP failover created a large burst of token refreshes causing transient restarts; the KMS rotation worker has no strong leader election or idempotency for overlapping rotations and assumed audit delivery guarantees; the audit-sink replay path had a backward-incompatible schema change rolled in a previous release that made replay abort when receiving older event variants. The combination produced rotated keys without durable audit entries and a gap in compliance observability.
impact_summary: Missing audit entries for control-plane key rotations and related lifecycle events for ~3 hours across 12 service principals. Potential compliance exposure for SOC2 / ISO audits. No customer data exfiltration detected. Some internal automation depending on audit-derived signals (alerting, downstream cleanup) was delayed or mis-triggered.
action_items: Owner: Evan Kim - Emergency: add idempotency and preflight checks to KMS rotation worker. Ensure rotation attempts are gated on successful audit enqueue confirmation. Target: 2026-03-21

Owner: Asha Nair - Fix: revert/patch replay schema handling in audit-sink to accept legacy event_v1 payloads and include schema compatibility tests. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/audit-sink/pull/182. Target: 2026-03-17

Owner: Marc Liu - Reliability: implement leader election and in-progress marker for rotation jobs to avoid parallel partial rotations. Include e2e test that simulates IdP-induced restarts. Target: 2026-03-28

Owner: Priya Shah - Observability: add per-rotation audit delivery metrics and an SLO/alert that fires when enqueue-to-store latency > 2m or when replay fails. Dashboard: internal.redwood.com/dashboards/audit-pipeline. Target: 2026-03-18
Owner: Security (Daniel Ortiz) - Compliance: prepare an evidence package listing affected keys, affected time window, reconciliation steps and notify SOC team and auditors. Target: 2026-03-16

Owner: Product (Leah Morgan) - Communication: draft customer-facing summary for enterprise tenants impacted by audit gaps (if requested by compliance). Coordinate messaging with legal. Target: 2026-03-19
Owner: SRE (Evan Kim) - Runbook: update incident runbook for SSO failover scenarios to include immediate suspension of KMS rotations and step-by-step audit-sink validation. Target: 2026-03-15
Owner: Engineering Tools (Rakesh Patel) - Test: add synthetic tests that exercise IdP failovers + rotation windows in CI to catch regressions. Target: 2026-04-04
status_updates: 2026-03-11 09:00 UTC - Sofia P: Created ticket after preliminary incident review. Notified Compliance and Legal. Assigned to Evan.

2026-03-12 14:30 UTC - Evan K: Completed initial triage, validated that no customer PII was affected. Implemented temporary guard to prevent rotation worker from starting while audit-sink replay is in 'error' state.
2026-03-13 11:20 UTC - Asha N: Opened PR to add backward-compat parsing and unit tests (PR #182). Requesting design review from runtime team.

2026-03-14 16:05 UTC - Marc L: Prototype leader-election for rotation worker using DynamoDB lease; benchmarked with concurrent rotation attempts. Results: single leader prevents partial double-rotations. Proposal ready for review.
2026-03-14 17:30 UTC - Compliance: Received initial reconciliation artifact; request for more granular per-key attestations noted as action item
decisions_and_tradeoffs: Short-term: Deploy a backward-compatible parser in audit-sink to unblock replay quickly rather than reverting the schema change (tradeoff: adds technical debt but minimizes compliance exposure).
Mid-term: Add idempotency and leader-election to rotation worker instead of introducing complex global locks. This favors operational simplicity and scalability.
Long-term: Consider moving rotation coordination into control plane with transaction semantics tied to audit-store confirmations (higher engineering cost; planned Q3 2026).
verification_plan: Stage: unit/integration - audit-sink PR must include compatibility test vectors for v1 and v2 events
Stage: staging - run a simulated IdP failover while a scheduled rotation is in-flight and assert no partial rotations and all audit events delivered
Stage: canary - deploy rotation leader-election to 10% of traffic and validate metrics for 48h
Stage: production - enable global rollout with automatic monitoring that blocks rotation windows if audit enqueue latency or replay errors exceed thresholds
followups: Track ENG-14887 (audit-store retention policy) - ensure retention covers replay and reconciliation windows
Schedule compliance tabletop to review incident and update audit SLAs - lead: Maria Gonzales
Add a recurring quarterly drill for combined SSO failover + rotation scenario
Post-deployment review meeting to confirm all action items closed and evidence artifacts uploaded to Confluence
notes: This incident highlighted a subtle assumption: rotation worker assumed that audit delivery was 'at least once' and durable within rotation window; we must not depend on eventual delivery for security-critical operations.
We prioritized reconciliation and stopping further risk over immediate rollbacks to preserve evidence for auditors.
Eng teams should coordinate schema changes to ingestion pipelines with a strict compatibility checklist and a staging replay verification step.
